name: Nanjing Golden Eagle International Group
desc: Nanjing conglomerate founded in 1992 operating Golden Eagle department stores, mainly in Jiangsu, plus property development and car servicing.

name: Costa Cruises
desc: Italian cruise line owned by Carnival Corporation, sailing about eight ships mainly in the Mediterranean, Northern Europe and South America.

name: Oterra
desc: Danish producer of natural colours from plants, fruits and vegetables for food and beverage manufacturers, serving customers in more than 110 countries.

name: GMO
desc: Boston investment manager (Grantham, Mayo, Van Otterloo) known for contrarian, valuation-driven strategies.

name: Cook Medical
desc: Privately held US maker of minimally invasive medical devices, part of Cook Group, serving customers in about 135 countries.

name: Delpharm
desc: French contract development and manufacturing organisation producing solid, sterile, semi-solid and liquid medicines for drug companies in Europe and North America.

name: Fareva
desc: French contract manufacturer producing pharmaceuticals, APIs, cosmetics, make-up and household products for brand owners from more than 40 sites.

name: Klüh Service Management
desc: Düsseldorf multi-service provider offering security, cleaning, catering, clinic and airport services to clients in six countries.

name: Veronesi Holding
desc: Italian family-owned food group behind the AIA poultry and Negroni cured-meat brands and Veronesi animal feed.

name: Capri Sun Group Holding
desc: Swiss owner of the Capri-Sun juice-drink pouch brand, privately held by Hans-Peter Wild, produced in 24 countries and sold in over 100.

name: Flossbach von Storch
desc: Cologne asset manager founded in 1998 by Bert Flossbach and Kurt von Storch, managing multi-asset and equity funds for German investors.

name: Blackhawk Network
desc: Branded payments company distributing gift, prepaid and incentive cards through retailers and digital channels, taken private by Silver Lake and P2.

name: Nationwide Building Society
desc: World's largest building society, a member-owned UK mutual offering mortgages, savings and current accounts, which acquired Virgin Money in 2024.

name: Catalent
desc: US contract development and manufacturing organisation for drugs, biologics and consumer-health products, taken private by Novo Holdings in December 2024.

name: Ovako
desc: Swedish maker of clean engineering steel bars, tubes and rings for bearing, transport and manufacturing customers, owned by Sanyo Special Steel.

name: Diptyque
desc: Parisian luxury fragrance and scented-candle house owned by private equity firm Manzanita Capital, with 124 boutiques worldwide.

name: Sompo International
desc: Bermuda-based specialty commercial insurance and reinsurance platform built from Endurance Specialty, bought by Sompo for US$6.3bn in 2017.

name: Capco
desc: London-based technology and management consultancy for financial services with 6,500+ staff in 32 offices, acquired by Wipro for USD 1.45bn in 2021.

name: CANPACK Group
desc: Polish-origin packaging maker of beverage cans, glass, metal closures and food packaging with nearly 8,500 staff at plants in 15 countries.

name: Van Cleef & Arpels
desc: Paris high-jewellery and watch house known for the Alhambra line, owned by Swiss luxury group Richemont since 1999.

name: Fujikin
desc: Unlisted Japanese maker of precision valves, fittings and fluid-control systems for semiconductor fabs, energy, aerospace and life-science plants.

name: Interzero
desc: German circular-economy services group, formed in 2022 from ALBA Group businesses including Interseroh, with about 2,000 staff in ten countries.

name: Aquent
desc: Boston creative and marketing staffing company founded in 1986, placing talent with clients such as Google, Microsoft, Nike and NASA.

name: Aspen Medical
desc: Canberra health-services contractor founded in 2003, running hospitals, defence and government medical services in Australia, the Pacific, Middle East and US.

name: Genki Forest
desc: Beijing-based maker of sugar-free sparkling water, teas and functional drinks, founded by Tang Binsen and selling in China and the US.

name: Heidenhain
desc: Foundation-owned German maker of precision linear and angle encoders, length gauges and TNC numerical controls for machine tools and semiconductor equipment.

name: Acome
desc: Worker-owned French cooperative making fibre-optic, copper and automotive wire and cable systems, synthetic tubes, from plants in France, China, Brazil and Morocco.

name: Skyline Enterprises
desc: New Zealand operator of gondola and luge tourist attractions in Queenstown and Rotorua, with luge sites built in Canada, Singapore, South Korea and Malaysia since 2003.

name: Kurtz Ersa
desc: Seventh-generation family-owned German maker of Ersa soldering and electronics-production machines, foam moulding machines and automation systems.

name: WorldQuant
desc: Quantitative investment management firm founded by Igor Tulchinsky, spun out of Millennium, focused on statistical arbitrage.

name: Hobby-Wohnwagenwerk
desc: Family-run German caravan and motorhome maker (Hobby, Fendt-Caravan) holding nearly 25% of the German and 15% of the European caravan market.

name: Schmalz
desc: Family-run German maker of vacuum grippers, vacuum components and ergonomic handling systems for automation and logistics.

name: Kögel
desc: Bavarian maker of semi-trailers, trailers and swap bodies, owned by Ulrich Humbaur, selling 13,000 vehicles in fiscal 2025.

name: Missoni
desc: Varese knitwear fashion house, 58.8% owned by the Missoni family and 41.2% by the state-backed fund FSI since 2018.

name: Bottomline Technologies
desc: Business payments, cash management and banking software provider serving nearly one million financial institutions and businesses in 92 countries.

name: La Sportiva
desc: Family-owned Italian maker of climbing shoes, mountain-running and mountaineering boots and outdoor apparel, with plants in Italy and China.

name: Ensinger
desc: Family-owned German maker of compounds, semi-finished stock, composites, technical parts and profiles in engineering and high-performance plastics.

name: Dream Games
desc: Istanbul developer of Royal Match and Royal Kingdom, ranked among the largest mobile game developers worldwide by revenue.

name: SAERTEX
desc: Family-owned German maker of non-crimp glass, carbon and aramid fabrics and composite systems for wind, aerospace, automotive and marine uses.

name: Banner Batterien
desc: Austrian family-run maker of starter and industrial batteries with 805 staff, EUR 270m revenue and 27 branches in 14 countries.
